stem.en: A bacterium is a hundred times smaller than a moong cell and has no inner rooms. Kabir says "so it must be starving or badly organised". Why does it get by?

text.en: At a hundredth the size, it has a hundred times more skin per bit of inside. Diffusion feeds every part in an instant, and it can run its chemistry in one room because nothing is far from anything.

feedback.en: Small cells are the best fed of all. Rooms are needed when a cell is big enough for its chemistries to need separating.
Its wall is the same bilayer, with a fence outside. Size does the work.
Leeuwenhoek watched them swim and divide. Simple is not dead.

explanation.en: Turn the surface rule around. Smaller means more skin per inside, so a tiny cell is fed everywhere at once and needs no rooms.
